sentences.text: 2  JUDGMENT
Though these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, they are taken up for final disposal.

These appeals are filed against the judgment and award dated 01.09.2016 passed in MVC No.254/2013 by the III Addl. Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Vijayapura (for short 'Tribunal').
2.
Though this matter is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.
4. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.

5. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer submits that the jurisdictional police have received the information about the accident from Gaurav Hospital on 30/11/2012, the FIR was delayed registered after 12 days i.e. on 12/12/2012.
The spot Mahazar was conducted on 01/12/2012 without registering the FIR.
That the petitioner had admitted in the hospital, the history of assault, but not the accident.
The Tribunal mistook this point and over looked Ex.P9 and wrongly appreciated on record and sought for dismissal of the appeal.

(c) What order or award?
7.

My answers to the above points are;
(a) Point No.1: Partly affirmative.

(b) Point No.2: In the negative.
 (c) Point No.3: As per final order

.

sentences.text: With regard to the enhancement of compensation is concerned, the petitioner has produced Ex.P7 the discharge card and wound certificate at Ex.P9 which reveals that petitioner had sustained fracture of union of deformity with lower end fracture of upper end, right tibia grade-IIC, # lower pole of right patella and other injuries.
The x-ray report also reveals the similar facts.
According to doctor, these injuries are grievous in nature.

9. The petitioner also examined one Dr.Gurunath Kulkarni, through the Court Commissioner who has been examined as PW.2 and examined the injured on 26.03.2015, wherein he has stated there is a fracture of right tibia, proximal 1/3rd with non union with rapture of patellar tendon.

Disability noted that mobility component, loss of knee function 50 x 3 = 15%.
10.
The tribunal has assessed the disability at 15% to the whole body which is just and proper.
However, the tribunal has taken the notional income of the injured petitioner at Rs.5,000/- instead of Rs.6,500/- as as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The petitioner is aged about 39 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '11'.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,28,700/- (Rs.6,500/- x 12 x 11 x 15%) on account of 'loss of future income'.
Accordingly, the same is rounded off to Rs.1,29,000/-.

11. Considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment, disability and medical expenses, I am of the considered opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re-determined and re-calculated as under:-
Sl. Awarded by the Enhanced by this  Heads No Tribunal Court 1

Towards pain and suffering Rs.20,000/- Rs.30,000/-
2 Medical expenses incurred and Rs.2,30,000/- Rs.2,30,000/-
 future medical expenses,
 attendant, conveyance,
 nourishing food, and other  incidental charges  (Rs.2,10,000 + Rs.20,000)
3 Loss of income during laid up Rs.15,000/- Rs.20,000/-
 period 4 Loss of future income of Rs.99,000/- Rs.1,29,000/-
 permanent disability 5 Loss of amenities, Life Rs.15,000/- Rs.25,000/-
 comforts and expectancy of  life  Total Rs.3,74,000/- Rs.4,34,000/-
12.

Thus, the petitioner in MFA No.200115/2017 is entitled compensation in a sum of Rs.4,34,000/-
as against Rs.3,74,000/- with interest at 6% p.a.

sentences.text: With regard to liability is concerned, the wound certificate/Ex.P9 does not disclose that the injured admitted to the Hospital with the history of assault as argued by the learned counsel appearing on behalf of insurance company.
Hence, in this regard, arguments advanced by the insurance company cannot be accepted.
Ex. P9
clearly reveals that this wound certificate/medico legal certificate issued by medical officer.
Mere non mentioning of the number is not a ground to reject the claim of the appellant.
The Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record including the delay in filing the FIR.

14. Keeping in mind the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Ravi vs. Badrinarayan and others reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693 and considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the considered view that the appellant/insurance company in MFA No.201943/2016 have not made out grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award as to the liability of the insurance company.

entities.text: Ravi vs. Badrinarayan and others reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693

sentences.text:
Hence, I answered point No.2 in Negative.
15.

For the aforesaid reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) MFA No.200115/2017 filed by the petitioner/claimant is allowed in part.
ii) MFA No.201943/2016 filed by the insurance company is dismissed.
iii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.4,34,000/- as against Rs.3,74,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.

iv) Respondent/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
v) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
vi) The amount in deposit, if any, by the insurance company shall be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal, along with TCR and a copy of this order.
Sd/-
